# Pharmacoeconomic Evaluation: Daily Ruxolitinib vs. Twice-Weekly Tacrolimus Maintenance

**The Vitiligo Initiative | Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR)**  
**Outcome 4:** Safe and Reachable | **Outcome 3:** Durability ([`docs/durability/maintenance-trial-concept.md`](../durability/maintenance-trial-concept.md))  
**Data Reference:** [`docs/durability/data/maintenance-cost.json`](../durability/data/maintenance-cost.json) | Generated by `scripts/durability/maintenance_cost.py`

---

## Executive Summary

While topical ruxolitinib 1.5% cream (Opzelura) achieves ~50% F-VASI75 at 52 weeks, stopping treatment results in loss of response in ~42% of patients within 12 months (TRuE-V long-term extension, [NCT04530344](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04530344)). 
However, **continuous indefinite twice-daily application costs over $14,600 / year in the US and £2,600 / year in the UK**, creating severe access hurdles and lifetime payer strain.

A proactive step-down to **twice-weekly generic tacrolimus 0.1% ointment** maintains response via calcineurin inhibition at:
- **$45 / year in the US (99.7% cost reduction; savings of $14,613 per patient-year)**
- **£31.50 / year in England (98.8% cost reduction; savings of £2,596 per patient-year)**
- **Reduces the cost per relapse prevented from $86,224 to $265 (a 325-fold improvement in cost-effectiveness)**

## 3. Cost-Effectiveness & Relapse Prevention Metrics

From the TRuE-V randomized withdrawal evidence ([`docs/durability/README.md`](../durability/README.md)):
- 1-Year Relapse Rate upon stopping ($P_{\text{stop}}$): **42.0%**
- 1-Year Relapse Rate on maintained therapy ($P_{\text{maintain}}$): **25.0%**
- Absolute Risk Reduction ($\text{ARR}$): $42.0\% - 25.0\% = \mathbf{17.0\%}$
- Number Needed to Treat ($\text{NNT}$): $1 / 0.17 = \mathbf{5.88}$ (approx. 6 patients must receive maintenance for 1 year to avert 1 relapse)

### Incremental Cost per Relapse Prevented (1-Year Horizon)

$$\text{Cost per Relapse Averted} = \text{Annual Regimen Cost} \times \text{NNT}$$

| Regimen | Cost per Relapse Prevented (US) | Cost per Relapse Prevented (UK) | Incremental Cost-Effectiveness |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Continuous Daily Ruxolitinib** | **$86,223.53** | **£15,458.82** | Highly costly; exceeds standard willingness-to-pay thresholds for maintenance |
| **Twice-Weekly Ruxolitinib** | **$12,317.65** | **£3,864.71** | Moderate cost |
| **Twice-Weekly Tacrolimus** | **$264.71** | **£185.29** | **Dominant strategy:** >325× more cost-effective |

## 4. Clinical & Translational Implications

1. **Trial Concept Feasibility ([`docs/durability/maintenance-trial-concept.md`](../durability/maintenance-trial-concept.md)):**
   - The proposed investigator-initiated double-blind randomized trial (twice-weekly tacrolimus 0.1% vs vehicle) can be executed with negligible per-patient investigational drug costs (~$45/patient/year).
   - If tacrolimus preserves repigmentation with a hazard ratio $\text{HR} \approx 0.50$, it establishes a scalable, globally accessible standard of care that low- and middle-income countries can afford.
2. **Payer Strategy (NICE, Medicare, Commercial Insurers):**
   - Current NICE guidelines ([TA1140](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta1140)) require strict prior authorization due to ruxolitinib's £657/tube list price.
   - Recommending a step-down protocol after achieving F-VASI75 (switch to twice-weekly generic tacrolimus) allows health systems to fund induction therapy while protecting public drug budgets against runaway chronic maintenance expenditure.
3. **Safety Optimization (Boxed Warnings & Cumulative Exposure):**
   - Stepping down from daily JAK inhibition to twice-weekly topical calcineurin inhibitor reduces annual JAK exposure by 85–100%, mitigating theoretical long-term safety concerns regarding continuous immunosuppression.
